item.title: Shinshu Soba & Nagano Food Guide: What to Eat in the Japan Alps
item.description: Nagano Prefecture has one of the most distinctive regional food traditions in Japan — shaped by a landlocked mountain climate, heavy snowfall, intense cold, and the need to preserve food through long winters. The absence of a coastline drove the development of an extraordinary preserved-food culture: lacto-fermented vegetables (tsukemono), long-aged miso from locally grown soybean and barley, smoke-dried mountain trout and carp, dried mushrooms and wild vegetables gathered from the alpine forests.
